{{Quote|We'll rebuild ''[Mandalore]''. Isn't that our history? For thousands of years, we have been on the verge of extinction, and for thousands of years we have survived.|Din Djarin|<ref name="Ch. 23">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 23: The Spies}}</ref>}}
The '''Mandalorians'''—known in ''[[Mando'a]]'' as the '''''Mando'ade''''' ("'''Children of Mandalore'''")—were a [[Mandalorian clan|clan]]-based culture composed of members from multiple [[species]] and bound by a common [[Mandalorian Creed|creed]], [[Mando'a|language]], and [[Mandalorian code|code]]. Known primarily as highly-effective [[Mercenary|mercenaries]] and [[bounty hunter]]s, Mandalorians as a socio-cultural group have at various points in [[The galaxy|galactic]] history played a major role as legendary [[Soldier|warriors]] and conquerors.

Originating around the year [[9991 BBY]] on the [[planet]] of [[Mandalore]] in the [[galaxy]]'s [[Outer Rim Territories]], the Mandalorians' way of life revolved around honor and war, being led by a sole ruler known as the [[Mandalore (title)|Mand'alor]], whose [[Journeyman Protector|Protectors]] maintained a relative state of peace and unity between their people's warrior clans. As a result of their warrior culture, the Mandalorians launched several [[Wars of Mandalorian expansion|wars of expansion]] by the time of the [[Old Republic-era]], [[Mandalorian crusades|colonizing]] nearby worlds such as [[Krownest]], [[Ordo]], and [[Concord Dawn]], leading the [[sector]] surrounding their homeworld to be known as [[Mandalore sector|Mandalorian Space]].

Throughout their history, several prominent groups of Mandalorian warriors came into existence, such as [[Mandalorian crusaders]], [[rally master]]s, and [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]], all of whom waged war [[Mandalorian-Galactic Republic war|on]] the [[Galactic Republic]] [[Mandalorian-Jedi War|and]] the [[Jedi Order]]. According to legends, many of these conflicts involved a Mand'alor who went by the name of [[Mandalore the Great]].

In spite of this, relations between the Mandalorians and the [[Jedi]] were not always hostile, as [[Tarre Vizsla]], a [[human]] Mandalorian, was inducted into the Jedi Order as a [[Youngling|child]], creating a [[lightsaber]] known as the [[Darksaber]] around the [[Standard year|year]] [[1,050 BBY|1050 BBY]]. Tarre eventually founded [[House Vizsla]], claiming the position of Mand'alor, with the Darksaber becoming a symbol of leadership for both House Vizsla and the Mandalorian people as a whole.

However, after Vizsla's death, members of his [[Mandalorian house|house]] [[Sacking of the Jedi Temple|raided]] the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] during the [[fall of the Old Republic]], stealing the Darksaber and using it to reunify the Mandalorian people, waging war once more on the Jedi Order. Unfortunately, the final conflict between the Mandalorian [[warlord]]s and the Jedi at the planet Mandalore led to a [[Annihilation|cataclysm]] that turned much of its surface into a lifeless [[Color|white]] desert, rendering it uninhabitable outside of [[Hermit|hermetically]] sealed dome cities. After their defeat, the Mandalorians remained isolated in their sector well into the [[High Republic Era]], not attempting to wage another war on either the Jedi or the Republic, with which they coexisted through [[Republic–Mandalore treaty|treaties]]. However, the Mandalorians' warrior ways and desire for conquest remained alive, eventually leading to infighting and [[Mandalorian Civil Wars|civil wars]].

However, although Mandalore was still under control of traditional Mandalorian warriors, much of the planet's population had become part of a pacifist movement known as the [[New Mandalorians]], led by the young [[Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze]] of [[House Kryze]], with the traditionalist warriors being forced to use violence to hold on to power. Eventually, around the year [[42 BBY]], a [[Great Clan Wars|civil war]] broke out between the pacifist New Mandalorian movement and the [[martial traditionalists]], who wished to maintain their warrior heritage. Mandalore's capital of [[Keldabe]] was destroyed during the Mandalorian Civil War, and many [[Death|perished]] during the conflict, including Duke [[Adonai Kryze]], Satine's [[Parent|father]]. Satine herself had to remain under protection from the Jedi Order, as the traditionalists sent bounty hunters after her. However, Mandalore's traditionalist minority was eventually defeated during the war, being [[Exile (punishment)|exiled]] to Mandalore's moon of [[Concordia]]. While the [[Death Watch]], a traditionalist group under Mand'alor [[Pre Vizsla]], wished to retake their homeworld, the [[Old Mandalorians]] scattered across the galaxy as mercenaries.

During the [[Clone Wars]], members of the warrior culture would align themselves with both sides of the conflict, which was secretly orchestrated by the [[Sith]] Order, who hired the Mandalorian bounty hunter [[Jango Fett]] to become the [[clone template]] for the [[Grand Army of the Republic]], with Fett's [[Cloning|clones]] being trained by the Mandalorian Protectors, while the Death Watch briefly joined the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], in hopes of reclaiming Mandalore. Under the New Mandalorian government, Mandalore remained neutral and participated in the [[Council of Neutral Systems]] as a leading member. However thanks to being backed up by the criminal conglomerate known as the [[Shadow Collective]], Death Watch was able to [[Takeover of Mandalore|topple]] the ruling New Mandalorian regime, but the machinations of [[Maul]], leader of the Collective, led to another [[Mandalorian Civil War (19 BBY)|civil war]] among the Death Watch, which split into the Collective-backed [[Mandalorian super commando]]s, and the [[Mandalore resistance]], which was supported by the Republic. However, the conflict [[Siege of Mandalore|culminated]] in the [[Occupation of Mandalore|occupation]] of Mandalore by the Galactic Republic and its subsequent government, the [[Galactic Empire]], while Concord Dawn, the Protectors' [[Protectors Camp|headquarters]], was transformed into a [[Concord Dawn Protectorate|protectorate]].

Following the [[Proclamation of the New Order|rise]] of the Empire, [[Bo-Katan Kryze]] was made [[Regent]] of Mandalore, but she refused to follow [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]]. As a result, she was replaced with [[Gar Saxon]], a former Mandalorian super commando, who was installed as [[Viceroy]] over Mandalore, his rule enforced by the [[Imperial Super Commando]]s. As with many worlds in the galaxy, Mandalore was oppressed under [[Imperial Era|Imperial rule]], with weapons such as the [[Arc Pulse Generator]] being developed to pacify and rein in the war-like civilization, while the Mandalorian Protectors under [[Fenn Rau]] were forced to serve the Empire on Concord Dawn. However, during the [[Galactic Civil War]], the Empire's rule on Mandalore was opposed by the [[Mandalorian resistance]], which was supported by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]], and was also joined by Fenn Rau after the Protectors' destruction. After the deaths of Gar Saxon and his brother and successor, [[Governor]] [[Tiber Saxon]], Bo-Katan Kryze, after receiving the Darksaber from [[Sabine Wren]] of [[Clan Wren]], assumed the position of Mand'alor. Kryze united the Mandalorian resistance as another [[Mandalorian Civil War (Imperial Era)|civil war]] erupted on Mandalore, a part of the galaxy-wide struggle against Imperial rule. Kryze's reign as Mand'alor was short lived, however, and the Empire started the [[Great Purge of Mandalore]], killing millions of Mandalorians during the [[Night of a Thousand Tears]], while Kryze lost the Darksaber to [[Moff]] [[Gideon]].

After the [[Battle of Jakku|fall]] of the Empire and the [[New Republic Era|rise]] of the [[New Republic]], and following the Empire's Great Purge of Mandalore, the surviving Mandalorians went into hiding. One such group, [[the Tribe]], hid in a [[Nevarro Mandalorian covert|covert]] on [[Nevarro]]. The Tribe, which was secretly part of the [[Children of the Watch]], followed the [[Way of the Mandalore]], an ancient religion that had fallen out of mainstream Mandalorian society. However, the Tribe was forced to relocate after its members [[Incident on Nevarro|revealed]] themselves to protect one of their own, the bounty hunter [[Din Djarin]], from an [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|Imperial remnant]], which afterwards [[Attack on the Tribe|wiped out]] most of the Tribe's members. Djarin, who had been tasked with returning the [[Force-sensitive]] [[foundling]] [[Din Grogu|Grogu]] to the Jedi Order, was aided in his task by several notable individuals, including Bo-Katan Kryze, Mandalore's former ruler, and [[Boba Fett]], the son of Mandalorian bounty hunter Jango Fett.

After the [[Hunt for Grogu|hunt]] for Grogu was over, Djarin attempted to return to the Tribe, which had [[Mandalorian covert|relocated]] to the [[Glavis Ringworld]], only to be expelled by its members when they discovered that he had removed his helmet, which went against the Way of the Mandalore. Djarin and Fett joined forces once more, leading [[Fett gotra|Fett's]] [[gotra]] in its [[War against the Pykes|war]] against the [[Pyke Syndicate]], during which he was [[Battle of Mos Espa|reunited]] with Grogu, who had decided to rejoin him. Fett and Djarin eventually defeated the [[Pyke]]s, allowing Fett to establish himself as [[Tatooine]]'s reigning [[crime lord]], while Djarin and Grogu left the planet. Afterwards, Djarin was again accepted into the Tribe after traveling to Mandalore and bathing in the Living Waters to clear his transgression. In this same adventure, Bo-Katan also bathed and therefore was also unexpectedly welcomed as a member of the Tribe. However, the development allowed Kryze to walk both the path of the Way and unorthodox Mandalorian society, paving the way for her to reclaim the Darksaber and lead a united Mandalorian people in the [[Conflict on Mandalore|reconquest of Mandalore]].

==Society and culture==
===The Mandalorian people===
{{Quote|We are a people of tradition.|Satine Kryze|<ref name="Corruption">{{TCW|Corruption (episode)}}</ref>}}
[[File:BoKatanNightOwls-AFIN.jpg|thumb|left|300px|[[Death Watch]] flies into battle.]]
The Mandalorians—known in ''[[Mando'a]]'' as the ''Mando'ade'', which translated to "Children of Mandalore"<ref name="TOM 104">{{GermanFanCite|104|Database}}</ref>—were some of the most feared warriors in the galaxy.<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> As prideful warriors, they held combat as the cornerstone to their culture, their individual identity, and spirit.<ref name="TSWB">''[[The Star Wars Book]]''</ref> Mandalorians shared a strong [[Mandalorian code|code]]<ref name="Protector Episode gallery">{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/the-protector-of-concord-dawn-episode-gallery|text="The Protector of Concord Dawn" Episode Gallery}}</ref> of honor<ref name="Eminence" /> that could be invoked to settle disputes with one-on-one combat that would conclude with the death of one opponent.<ref name="The Protector of Concord Dawn" /> This affinity and tradition for single combat extended beyond justice, however, as Mandalorians even sought single combat simply for the glory of fighting a great opponent, such as a [[Jedi Knight]],<ref name="A Friend in Need" /> and even used it to settle leadership disputes. However, some in [[House Vizsla]] refused to accept non-Mandalorians like [[Maul]] from ever becoming ruler of Mandalore via such traditions. Maul himself had [[Prime Minister]] [[Almec]] lie to the Mandalorian people by claiming that Satine Kryze had killed [[Pre Vizsla]], Maul's predecessor.<ref name="ShadesofReason" />

The [[Darksaber]] was appropriated by House Vizsla as a symbol of authority and leadership used to unify the Mandalorians.<ref name="Trials of the Darksaber">{{Rebels|Trials of the Darksaber}}</ref> The weapon became revered and was passed down to new leaders who defeated the previous leader in combat, with claiming the weapon in any other way being considered illegitimate.<ref name="Legacy of Mandalore" /> As well as [[Galactic Basic Standard]], Mandalorians spoke Mando'a,<ref name="SabineSketchbook">''[[Sabine My Rebel Sketchbook]]''</ref> whose written form was also known as [[Mandalorian (writing system)|Mandalorian]].<ref name="The Academy Trivia Gallery">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/the-academy-trivia-gallery|text="The Academy" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 3}}</ref>

Mandalorian clan structure was like a pyramid,<ref name="RebelsRecon212">{{RebelsRecon|Ob90p0SoMpY|#2.19: Inside "The Mystery of Chopper Base" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/rebels-recon-inside-the-mystery-of-chopper-base}}</ref> with the ruler, or [[Mandalore (title)|Mand'alor]],<ref name="Creating Mandalore" /><ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> at the top and the Mandalorian Protectors enforcing their rule. Below them were the political factions known as [[Mandalorian house|houses]], which were made up of family [[Mandalorian clan|clans]].<ref name="RebelsRecon212" /> One example was House Vizsla, which was comprised of Clan Vizsla and Clan Wren.<ref name="The Protector of Concord Dawn" /> Under the rule of Duchess Satine Kryze and the New Mandalorian government during the [[Clone Wars]], the Mandalorians had mostly rejected their martial ancestral ways but maintained a [[Mandalorian Guard|police force]] and [[Mandalorian secret service|secret service]], who wielded [[electropole]]s and [[Shield (physical armor)|shields]].<ref name="Mandalorian Guard Databank">{{Databank|mandalorian-guard|Mandalorian Guard}}</ref>

[[File:Precious-Cargo-Card-Trader.png|thumb|right|250px|Mandalorians were known to adopt lost children, referred to as foundlings.]]
Though Mandalorians were usually distinctly human, one did not need to be human to become one. Instead, what one needed to do was follow the [[Mandalorian Creed]]. Thus, some individuals, non-humans included, could be adopted into the Mandalorian creed as [[foundling]]s, children raised to become [[Mandalorian warrior]]s.<ref name="SWCEUAE">''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref> Followers of the Creed viewed the foundlings as the future, and any Mandalorian with a foundling in their care was duty-bound to reunite it with their kind or to raise them, acting as the child's parent. When a foundling came of age, if he or she had not yet been reunited with its kind, they could decide to leave or join the Mandalorians,<ref name="Chapter 8" /> and become an [[Mandalorian apprentice|apprentice]]. According to Creed, saving a foundling was the highest honor.<ref name="Chapter 20">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 20: The Foundling}}</ref> Although Mandalorians who had been foundlings were treated no differently than any other Mandalorians, possessing the right to bear their [[Mandalorian armor|armor]]<ref name="Chapter 13">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 13: The Jedi}}</ref> and even to form their own clans,<ref name="Chapter 8" /> discrimination towards foundlings was observed to be present within Mandalorian organizations,<ref name="Chapter 1" /><ref name="Chapter 3">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 3: The Sin}}</ref><ref name="Chapter 8" /> including members of the Nite Owls, who said that former foundlings did not have Mandalorian blood in their veins.<ref name="Chapter 22">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 22: Guns for Hire}}</ref>

Several notable foundlings included [[Din Grogu|Grogu]]<ref name="Chapter 8" /> and [[Din Djarin]],<ref name="Chapter 1" /> both of [[Clan Mudhorn]],<ref name="Chapter 8" /> as well as the famed Mandalorian [[bounty hunter]]<ref name="WOTBH IG-88">[[War of the Bounty Hunters – IG-88 1|''War of the Bounty Hunters – IG-88'' 1]]</ref> [[Jango Fett]].<ref name="Chapter 14">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 14: The Tragedy}}</ref> Orthodox Mandalorians,<ref name="TSWB" /> such as the [[Children of the Watch]], followed ancient religions such as the [[Way of the Mandalore]]. Mandalorians who followed the Way did not consider others as true Mandalorians, while mainstream Mandalorian regarded the Children of the Watch as religious zealots.<ref name="Chapter 11" /> [[Pog soup]] was a traditional food of the Mandalorian people, yet Child of the Watch Din Djarin had never tasted it before meeting non-Child [[Bo-Katan Kryze]], much to her amusement.<ref name="Ch. 18">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 18: The Mines of Mandalore}}</ref>

===Gear, combat, and art===
{{Quote|Ezra, the armor I wear is five hundred years old. I reforged it to my liking, but the battles, the history, the blood all lives within it. And the same goes for every Mandalorian.''"<br />"''This armor is part of our identity. It makes us Mandalorians who we are.|Sabine Wren and Alrich Wren|<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" />}}
[[File:Sabines_Armor_AR.png|thumb|left|250px|Sabine Wren, a Mandalorian warrior and artist.]]
The Mandalorian Din Djarin remarked that weapons were a part of a Mandalorian's religion on more than one occasion.<ref name="Return of the Mandalorian" /><ref name="Chapter 2">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 2: The Child}}</ref> The Jedi [[Kanan Jarrus]] once complained that Mandalorians only seemed to solve problems by shooting.<ref name="The Protector of Concord Dawn" /> The young Mandalorian [[Sabine Wren]], a friend of Jarrus's, once declared it was a bad idea to get between "a Mandalorian and a weapons package."<ref name="Wings of the Master">{{Rebels|Wings of the Master}}</ref>

[[Mandalorian armor]] developed a legendary reputation that was feared across the galaxy<ref name="DeathWatchDB" /> and was visually distinctive with its honeycomb plate patterns and menacing T-shaped visors. The [[armor]] was made of [[beskar]], a metal extremely resistant to damage and malleable enough to be forged into armor.<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" /> The signature innovation of the Mandalorians was the mining and tempering of beskar. The metal was found only on Mandalorian worlds.<ref name="TSWB" /> An ancient tradition and vital part of Mandalorian culture was forging the beskar into armor, which was carried out by [[Mandalorian Armorer]]s,<ref name="The Armorer">{{Databank|the-armorer|the Armorer}}</ref> who could also forge beskar into other gear like [[whistling bird]]s.<ref name="Chapter 3" /> Beskar was also used to forge weapons such as [[crushgaunt]]s and [[beskad]]s.<ref name="Collapse">''[[Collapse of the Republic]]''</ref>

On top of the fabled armor, Mandalorian warriors were equipped with anti-Jedi tools such as [[jetpack]]s, [[magnet]]ized boots, [[heads-up display]]s, and [[Mandalorian vambrace|vambraces]]<ref name="AEYKTKUAE">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]''</ref> that featured weaponry and tools designed to combat the Force abilities of the Jedi.<ref name="Mandalorian Vambraces">{{Databank|mandalorian-vambraces|Mandalorian Vambraces}}</ref> Some of this weaponry not only helped combat but outright mimicked Jedi abilities, such as their wrist-mounted sonic [[Repulsorlift|repulsors]] that knocked objects away like a Force push would.<ref name="Trials of the Darksaber" /> One popular piece of weaponry among the Mandalorians by the time of the Imperial Era was the [[WESTAR-35 blaster pistol]]s produced by [[Concordian Crescent Technologies]].<ref>{{Facebook|username=starwarsrebels|url=starwarsrebels/photos/a.230754950414469.1073741828.180356405454324/337107259779237/?type=1&permPage=1|name=Star Wars Rebels|date=August 20, 2014|quote=Sabine's blasters are a popular model on Mandalore, but like all of Sabine's gear, they're custom painted.|archivedate=20200810071803}}</ref> Other weaponry wielded by Mandalorians included the [[MT-97]] pistols produced by [[Mandalore Technologies]]<ref name="Hunters">''[[Star Wars: Hunters]]''</ref> and the [[GALAAR-15 blaster carbine]]. The [[JT-12 jetpack]]<ref name="MandalorePlot" /> and [[Z-6 jetpack]],<ref name="Z-6 Jetpack Databank">{{Databank|z-6-jetpack|Z-6 Jetpack}}</ref> which both could launch [[missile]]s, were used by the Mandalorians.<ref name="MandalorePlot" /><ref name="Z-6 Jetpack Databank" /> The [[Rising Phoenix]] was the training Mandalorians undertook to enhance their jetpack skills.<ref name="Chapter 8" /> The archetypal Mandalorian [[starfighter]] design was called the [[Kom'rk-class fighter/transport|''Kom'rk''-class fighter/transport]].<ref name="Gauntlet Fighter Databank">{{Databank|gauntlet-fighter|Gauntlet Fighter}}</ref>

The Mandalorians were very protective of their armor and the beskar, claiming that it belonged only to them and refusing to give it to anyone not related to the warrior culture The Mandalorian warrior Din Djarin only allowed [[Boba Fett]] to retake possession of [[Boba Fett's armor|his familial Mandalorian armor]] after learning that Fett was of Mandalorian heritage. However, despite the Mandalorians' claim that both their armor and beskar belonged only to them,<ref name="Chapter 14" /> several non-Mandalorians, such as the [[crime lord]] [[Dryden Vos]],<ref name="TOG">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]''</ref> [[Trandoshan]] [[big game hunter]] [[Garnac]],<ref name="Wookiee Hunt">{{TCW|Wookiee Hunt}}</ref> and [[Tempest Runner]] [[Lourna Dee]]<ref name="Tempest Runner">''[[The High Republic: Tempest Runner]]''</ref> had Mandalorian armor in their possession. Furthermore, Boba Fett's infamy led to several bounty hunters emulating the skilled [[mercenary]] by wearing knockoff Mandalorian armor, since knockoff Mandalorian gear was in no short supply in the [[bounty]] hunter profession.<ref name="SaV" />

Additionally, some non-Mandalorian individuals also sported beskar equipment, such as [[Enfys Nest]], who had beskar vambraces,<ref name="SWCEUAE" /> and a [[unidentified Arcona bounty hunter]], who wore a set of beskar armor.<ref name="Bounty Hunters 6">[[Bounty Hunters 6|''Bounty Hunters'' 6]]</ref> Despite not wearing a full set of Mandalorian armor, bounty hunter [[Carib Diss]] possessed a vambrace equipped with whistling birds.<ref name="TROS VD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> During her alliance with Mandalorians, [[Ahsoka Tano]] was given beskar equipment.<ref name="OFNF Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/old-friends-not-forgotten-episode-guide|text="Old Friends Not Forgotten" Episode Guide | The Clone Wars}}</ref> 

[[File:Pre_Vizsla_Darksaber_SW.png|thumb|right|270px|Mand'alor Pre Vizsla, leader of the Death Watch, wielding the Darksaber.]]
Mandalorian warriors possessed advanced combat training<ref name="AEYKTKUAE" /> from their many wars that were dated prior to the Republic's existence.<ref name="Imperial Super Commandos" /> However, it was not until their conflicts with the Jedi that they developed their signature combat style.<ref name="Star Wars Rebels Showrunner Explains Major Knight of the Old Republic Reference">{{WebCite|url=http://comicbook.com/starwars/2017/02/18/star-wars-rebels-knights-of-the-old-republic-reference-confirmed|text=Star Wars Rebels Showrunner Explains Major Knight of the Old Republic Reference|author=Lucas Siegel|archivedate=20170220002112}}</ref> This style entailed a Mandalorian utilizing a mix of melee, ranged, and [[Unarmed combat|hand-to-hand]] techniques<ref name="ShadesofReason" /> while incorporating technology into their vambraces to surprise a Jedi Knight in combat, allowing the Mandalorian to finish the Jedi off.<ref name="Complete Season Three TOD">[[Star Wars Rebels: Complete Season Three|''Star Wars Rebels'': Complete Season Three]], "Trials of the Darksaber" DVD commentary</ref> Mandalorian warriors continued to utilize this style of combat against the Jedi for some time as well as against other opponents.<ref name="Complete Season Three RTM">[[Star Wars Rebels: Complete Season Three|''Star Wars Rebels'': Complete Season Three]], "Return to Mandalore" Featurette</ref> They were also known to perform headbutts<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> known as [[Keldabe kiss]]es, a term which shared its name with Mandalore's former capital of [[Keldabe]].<ref name="FF">{{FactFile2014|98|MAN 1-4|Mandalore}}</ref><ref name="FLT" />

The Darksaber became a feared weapon in the days of the [[Galactic Republic|Old Republic]] as Mandalorian warriors of House Vizsla used it to slay many Jedi.<ref name="MandalorePlot" /> When the Jedi claimed the weapon and stored it in the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]], Mandalorian warriors would [[Sacking of the Jedi Temple|raid]] the Temple to reclaim the weapon that had become a symbol of their warrior ways.<ref name="Trials of the Darksaber" /> During the Clone Wars, the weapon also came to symbolize leadership of Death Watch as well as House Vizsla.<ref name="MandalorePlot" />

[[Mandalorian cubism|Cubism]] was a popular Mandalorian art movement during the Clone Wars. After the war, the paintings that had depicted the awfulness of war were used to promote and glorify it instead.<ref name="SabineSketchbook" /> Mandalorians typically trended towards strong angled and hexagonal lines, such as diamond and honeycomb shapes, in their architecture, vehicles, clothing, and even haircuts.<ref name="Creating Mandalore" /> The Darksaber notably reflected this style, with an angular pommel, hand guard, and [[blade emitter]].<ref name="Trials of the Darksaber" /> Sabine Wren, a Mandalorian and a member of the [[Spectres]], was a talented [[graffiti]] [[artist]] who personalized and painted her armor.<ref name="SabineSketchbook" /> A statue of Tarre Vizsla was erected on Mandalore and became a symbol for hope and Mandalorian history. When the Empire constructed an outpost on the statue, some Mandalorians saw this as offensive, eventually destroying the outpost to restore the emblematic statue's appearance.<ref name="Art History" /> Several Mandalorians decorated their [[beskar]] armor with their clan symbols.<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" /> In addition, some Mandalorian armor bore the [[mythosaur]] [[Bone|skull]] emblem,<ref name="FoD">''[[Forces of Destiny: Tales of Hope & Courage]]''</ref> one of the traditional symbols in Mandalorian iconography.<ref name="SabineSketchbook" />

==History==
{{Quote|Our people have suffered time and again. From division and squabbling factions. Mandalore has always been too powerful for any enemy to defeat. It is always our own division that destroys us.|Bo-Katan Kryze|<ref name="Ch. 23" />}}
===The Mandalorian crusades and early expansion===
{{Main|Mandalorian crusades}}
{{Quote|The Mandalorians have endured war since before the formation of the Republic.|Fenn Rau|<ref name="Imperial Super Commandos">{{Rebels|Imperial Supercommandos}}</ref>}}
[[File:MandalorianRallyMasterArmor-SaV.png|thumb|left|150px|A set of Mandalorian rally master armor.]]
Originating from the [[planet]] [[Mandalore]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]], around the year [[9991 BBY]],<ref name="Return of the Mandalorian" /> the Mandalorians' history was one of warriors who would become feared throughout [[the galaxy]], gaining a reputation as [[Mercenary|mercenaries]], [[bounty hunter]]s,<ref name="AEYKTKUAE" /> and warriors.<ref name="Chapter 6">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 6: The Prisoner}}</ref> In their past history, they were known to ride [[mythosaur]]s,<ref name="Chapter 1" /> with the mythosaur skull emblem also becoming one of the traditional symbols of Mandalorian iconography.<ref name="SabineSketchbook" /> Long before the [[Annihilation|Mandalorian cataclysm]], however, the creature was thought to have gone extinct.<ref name="BMF32">{{BuildFalconCite|32|Guide to the Galaxy}}</ref> Even prior to the formation of the modern Galactic Republic, war dominated their way of life,<ref name="Imperial Super Commandos" /> with their exploits creating the widely held belief that the Mandalorians were the greatest warriors in the galaxy.<ref name="Chapter 6" /> In interacting with the wider galaxy, the Mandalorians became a legendary people, who would play a major role in several generations of [[Timeline of galactic history|galactic history]].<ref name="224 Giveaway">{{InsiderCite|224|Prize Giveaway!}}</ref>

One group of Mandalorian warriors known as the [[Mandalorian crusaders]]<ref name="Nexus of Power" /> began waging [[Mandalorian crusades|war]] against other peoples to conquer their worlds.<ref name="Aliens of the Galaxy">''[[Star Wars: Aliens of the Galaxy]]''</ref><ref name="TOM 104" /> Armor-clad and wielding [[sword]]s,<ref name="TOM 104" /> the Mandalorians were open to laying waste to entire worlds during their crusades.<ref name="Aliens of the Galaxy" /> The crusaders conquered the planets of [[Krownest]] and [[Concord Dawn]],<ref name="TOM 104" /> a planet which would see great scars that included almost a third of its planetary mass fractured and reduced to space rubble.<ref name="The Protector of Concord Dawn" /> During the [[Old Republic-era]],<ref name="Note">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]'' establishes that [[Mandalorian rally master armor]] of the [[rally master]]s dated back to the [[Old Republic-era]]. ''[[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]'' establishes that the rally masters participated in [[Mandalorian]] wars of expansion, therefore, the Mandalorian wars of expansion must date to the Old Republic-era.</ref> Mandalorian [[rally master]]s, who wore distinct red [[Mandalorian rally master armor|armor]], served as battlefield [[commander]]s during the [[wars of Mandalorian expansion]].<ref name="Star Wars: Scum and Villainy">''[[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]''</ref>

[[File:TCW_Neo-Crusader_helmet.png|thumb|right|150px|The ancient helmet of a Mandalorian Neo-Crusader.]]
Eventually, the crusaders' expansion spread to the [[Inner Rim Territories|Inner Rim]], where they [[Devastation of Ubduria|devastated]] the planet [[Ubduria]] out of contempt for the [[Homeworld|native]] [[Ubdurian]]s, whom they viewed as dishonorable cowards.<ref name="Aliens of the Galaxy" /> In ancient times, a group of Mandalorian warriors known as the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]] existed.<ref name="WH TG" /> According to the [[Qel-Droma Epics]], at one point the Mandalorian Crusaders served under the command of the fallen [[Jedi Knight]] [[Ulic Qel-Droma]] out of the [[Iron Citadel]] on [[Empress Teta]], and rode [[Basilisk war droid]]s into combat.<ref name="Nexus of Power" /> Over the course of Mandalorian history, a united Mandalore proved to be too powerful for any outside enemy to defeat. However, it was division amongst the Mandalorian people and ensuing infighting that always brought about their downfall.<ref name="Ch. 23" />

===War against the Jedi===
{{Main|Mandalorian-Jedi War}}
{{Quote|I know that these commandos fought in many wars, often against the Jedi.|Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="MandalorePlot" />}}
[[File:Mandalore_mural.jpg|thumb|left|300px|A Mandalorian mural depicting the crusaders battling the Jedi.]]
The Mandalorian crusaders' expansion eventually brought them into [[Mandalorian-Jedi War|conflict]] with the [[Jedi Order]] and the Republic they protected.<ref name="Shades of Reason Trivia Gallery">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/shades-of-reason-trivia-gallery|text="Shades of Reason" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slides 3 and 4}}</ref> According to ancient songs, [[Mandalore the Great]], who held the title of Mand'alor, was involved in the conflict.<ref name="Chapter 8" /> Their first confrontations with the Jedi Knights took the Mandalorians by surprise: their use of [[the Force]] and the [[Force power|powers]] it [[Force-sensitive|granted]] them were a challenge that they had never encountered before. However, the prideful nature of the Mandalorians would not allow that disadvantage to stand, and they began to devise ways to overcome the powers of the enigmatic Jedi. The result was a major advancement in the development of Mandalorian technology, specifically their arsenal and their infamous armor. They also developed a fighting style that combined their entire arsenal and skills to allow them to counteract the Jedi's supernatural abilities.<ref name="Star Wars Rebels Showrunner Explains Major Knight of the Old Republic Reference" /> With these new technologies, the Mandalorians began to win their share of conflicts with the Jedi, and their warriors earned the reputation of being capable of confronting and defeating Jedi Knights.<ref name="Complete Season Three TOD" /><ref name="AEYKTKUAE" /> The generations-long conflict ensured an enmity that lasted for several wars and was remembered by the wider galaxy even millennia later during the Clone Wars. These clashes between the Mandalorians and the Jedi Order became immortalized through cubist [[Mandalorian mural|murals]] displayed in Mandalore's capital city of [[Sundari]] and on the moon [[Concordia]].<ref name="MandalorePlot" />

[[File:Tarre_Vizsla.png|thumb|right|250px|Tarre Vizsla, Mandalorian Jedi.]]
Despite their near-continuous conflicts, the Mandalorians and the Jedi were not always in conflict. The most prominent example of this was when the Mandalorian-born [[Tarre Vizsla]], founder of the powerful House Vizsla,<ref name="Return of the Mandalorian" /> was inducted into the Jedi Order as a child. True to his Mandalorian nature, Vizsla distinguished himself from his Jedi peers by creating a unique [[lightsaber]]: the [[Darksaber]]. At some point in his life, Tarre Vizsla became the Mand'alor, the sole ruler of Mandalore and a revered figure among his people. Following his death, the Jedi recovered the Darksaber and returned it to the Jedi Temple on [[Coruscant]].<ref name="Trials of the Darksaber" /> Mandalorians later honored Vizsla by building a large [[Statue of Tarre Vizsla|statue]] of him on Mandalore to cement his legacy.<ref name="Art History">{{FOD|Art History}}</ref>

During the [[Fall of the Old Republic|last centuries of the Old Republic]], the Mandalorians struck at the very heart of their enemies' power: members of [[Mandalorian house|House]] Vizsla [[Sacking of the Jedi Temple|infiltrated]] the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant]] and stole<ref name="MandalorePlot" /> Tarre Vizsla's Darksaber. They used the saber to conquer the entirety of Mandalore, and united the diverse houses and clans throughout their territory.<ref name="Trials of the Darksaber" />

===Decline===
====The devastation of Mandalore====
{{Main|Annihilation}}
{{Quote|Once upon a time, these plains were covered with grass. But I never saw it. This destruction happened before I was born.|Sabine Wren|<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" />}}
[[File:Journeyman_Protector-SW_Card_Trader.png|thumb|left|250px|A member of the Journeyman Protectors, Mandalorian lawmen who were part of the Mandalorian Protectors.]]
Despite the unity that House Vizsla had brought to Mandalore,<ref name="Trials of the Darksaber" /> such was the warrior temperament of the Mandalorians that it did not last. Constant warfare and relentless campaigns of conquest ravaged Mandalore. [[Warlord]]s from various clans emerged to fight the Jedi, but also to fight among themselves. The last great struggle between the Mandalorian warlords and the Jedi occurred on Mandalore itself, and caused a [[Annihilation|cataclysmic event]] that devastated the planet, scorching much of its surface into a lifeless, white [[desert]].<ref name="Creating Mandalore">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Two]] Featurette: "Creating Mandalore"</ref>

This event ended the war between the Mandalorians and the Jedi, as well as the Mandalorians' dreams of expansion. As a result of their homeworld's devastation, a major focus on reconstruction occupied the warriors for a time; the uninhabitable conditions of Mandalore's surface forced them to adapt, just as they had adapted to the Jedi's use of the Force. Instead of abandoning Mandalore, they constructed sealed [[Domed city|dome cities]], such as the capital city of Sundari.<ref name="Mandalorian super commando">{{SWE|groups|mandalorian-super-commando|Mandalorian super commando}}</ref> Other Mandalorian clans chose to settle on worlds of the Mandalore sector, such as [[Clan Wren]] on the snow planet of Krownest,<ref name="Legacy of Mandalore" /> while the Mandalorian Protectors established a base on the [[third moon of Concord Dawn]].<ref name="Protectors DB">{{Databank|the-protectors|The Protectors}}</ref>

After the new Galactic Republic emerged as the dominant galactic government after the Jedi Order and Republic's [[Defeat of the Sith|final victory over the Sith]] in the last [[Jedi-Sith War]],<ref name="Star Wars Propaganda">''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]''</ref> the Mandalorians kept out of trouble<ref name="Light of the Jedi">''[[The High Republic: Light of the Jedi]]''</ref> even though the Mandalorians' warrior ways and desire for conquest remained alive.<ref name="MandalorePlot" /> As the [[High Republic Era]] began to progress, the Mandalorians did not cause trouble with the Republic. During the [[Battle of Kur]] in the High Republic Era, [[Admiral]] [[Pevel Kronara]] of the [[Republic Defense Coalition]] noted that the Mandalorians had been relatively peaceful since before his birth.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" />

====Pacifism====
{{Quote|Mandalore's violent past is behind us. All of our warriors were exiled to our moon, Concordia. They died out years ago.|Prime Minister Almec|<ref name="MandalorePlot" />}}
[[File:New_Mandalorian_ministry_council.png|thumb|right|250px|The New Mandalorian Ruling Council.]]
In the years prior to the [[Invasion of Naboo]], another conflict broke out between the Mandalorian people: the [[Great Clan Wars]]. The civil war was fought between competing ideals within Mandalorian society, including [[Martial traditionalists|traditionalists]] who supported Mandalore's warrior past and the [[New Mandalorians]], led by [[Satine Kryze]]. The new faction rejected the warrior past and hoped to embrace pacifism.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> Also involved were the Mandalorian Protectors of Concord Dawn, an elite group of warriors sworn to defend the [[Concord Dawn system]].<ref name="The Protector of Concord Dawn" /> At the end of the civil war, Satine Kryze ruled as the [[Duchess]] of Mandalore, and the warrior clans were exiled to Concordia.<ref name="MandalorePlot" /> Some of these clans became the Death Watch, plotting their coup against the new regime, while others left Concordia and resettled in other parts of the galaxy, becoming the [[Old Mandalorians]]. These Old Mandalorians started working as private mercenaries, with no interest in revenge.<ref name="FLT" />

At some point before [[32 BBY]],<ref name="Note2">"[[Chapter 14: The Tragedy]]" establishes that [[Jango Fett]] participated in the [[Mandalorian]] Civil Wars. As Fett [[Death|died]] in the [[First Battle of Geonosis]] which began the [[Clone Wars]], then the Mandalorian Civil Wars must have taken place prior to that conflict. Furthermore, [[Age of Republic - Jango Fett 1|''Age of Republic - Jango Fett'' 1]] depicts Fett in his [[Boba Fett's armor|Mandalorian armor]] when he was hired by [[Dooku|Darth Tyranus]], and {{BustCollectionCite|20|Character}} establishes that Fett first received his [[armor]] during the Mandalorian Civil Wars. As such, he must have been hired at some point after the wars.</ref> a series of conflicts known as the [[Mandalorian Civil Wars]] took place,<ref name="Chapter 14" /> in which the [[Mandalorian warrior|Mandalorian commando]]<ref name="Z-6 Jetpack">{{Databank|z-6-jetpack|Z-6 Jetpack}}</ref> and [[foundling]] Jango Fett participated.<ref name="Chapter 14" /> It was during the wars that the skilled warrior obtained his [[Boba Fett's armor|distinctive]] [[Mandalorian armor]].<ref name="Bust20">{{BustCollectionCite|20|Character}}</ref> While her ideals saw violent resistance from some Mandalorians, such as Death Watch,<ref name="Who's Boss">{{InsiderCite|224|Who's the Boss?}}</ref> Satine gradually rebuilt following the damages caused by the war. The considerable number of deaths had left Satine with a fierce hatred of violence, and she became a staunch pacifist. She reformed Mandalorian way of life. She also established a [[Mandalorian Government Council]] that had several [[minister]]s, a cabinet which was led by a Prime Minister.<ref name="Corruption" /> By the time of the Clone Wars, the position was occupied by Almec. Under her rule, Mandalore prospered and turned into a modern and peaceful society.<ref name="MandalorePlot" /> This new government also eventually joined the Galactic Republic.<ref name="Duchess of Mandalore">{{TCW|Duchess of Mandalore}}</ref>

====Advent of the Clone Wars====
[[File:JangoFett1-reveal-cover.jpg|thumb|left|240px|The famed Mandalorian bounty hunter Jango Fett, who served as the clone template for the Grand Army of the Republic.]]
In the final years of the Republic, Jango Fett was considered the best [[bounty hunter]] in [[the galaxy]].<ref name="Jango Databank">{{Databank|jango-fett|Jango Fett}}</ref> The Mandalorian bounty hunter's reputation<ref name="WOTBH IG-88" /> attracted the attention of the [[Sith]] Order, and he was offered to become the [[clone template]] for the [[Grand Army of the Republic]] on [[Kamino]].<ref name="Age of Republic">[[Age of Republic - Jango Fett 1|''Age of Republic - Jango Fett'' 1]]</ref> Fett accepted the offer, and the [[Kaminoan]] [[Cloning|cloners]] used his genetic material to create genetically modified [[clone trooper]]s,<ref name="AotC">{{Film|II}}</ref> as well as two unaltered clones, [[Omega]] and [[Boba Fett|Alpha]],<ref name="Bounty Lost">{{TBB|Bounty Lost}}</ref> the latter whom Jango would take as his son,<ref name="AotC" /> and name Boba Fett, teaching him their [[Fetts|family's]] trade.<ref name="Age of Republic" /> The Mandalorian armor Fett wore inspired [[Phase I clone trooper armor|that]] of the clone troopers. Additionally the Mandalorian Protectors also aided the [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] in training the clone troopers,<ref name="The Protector of Concord Dawn" /> with at least one of Fett's clones, [[Bacara]], being trained by an [[Unidentified ex-Journeyman Protector|ex-Journeyman Protector]].<ref name="Character Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]''</ref>

Fett's clones acted as the Republic's backbone during its war with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], a galaxy-wide conflict known as the [[Clone Wars]].<ref name="AotC" /> When the Clone Wars erupted, Satine Kryze made sure that Mandalore and the [[New Mandalorians]] remained neutral and continued to prosper. She then became leader<ref name="MandalorePlot" /> of the [[Council of Neutral Systems]], a [[Galactic Senate]] conglomerate<ref name="Rise">''[[Rise of the Separatists]]''</ref> of 1,500 star systems who wished to stay out of the conflict.<ref name="MandalorePlot" /> Nevertheless, both the Republic and CIS put heavy pressure on the Duchess to try and get her to join their respective side.<ref name="Who's Boss" />

===Resurrection===
{{Quote|Listen, Duchess. Do you hear the people? They cry out for change. Your weak-minded rule of Mandalore is at an end. The resurrection of our warrior past is about to begin!|Pre Vizsla, to Satine Kryze|<ref name="ShadesofReason">{{TCW|Shades of Reason}}</ref>}}
[[File:VizslaArmy.png|thumb|right|250px|Pre Vizsla's Death Watch allied with Count Dooku and the Separatists.]]
Unknown to the New Mandalorians, the Concordian [[governor]] Pre Vizsla revived the Mandalorian warrior culture as the Death Watch.<ref name="DeathWatchDB">{{Databank|death-watch|Death Watch}}</ref> Among the leadership of the group was Duchess Satine's sister, [[Bo-Katan Kryze]],<ref name="A Friend in Need">{{TCW|A Friend in Need}}</ref> the leader of the [[Nite Owls]], a group of elite female warriors.<ref name="The Lawless" /> Death Watch began committing [[terrorist]] acts against the pacifist regime, including attacks on Mandalore, on a [[Attack on a Republic cruiser|Republic cruiser]],<ref name="MandalorePlot" /> and on [[Kalevala]], a planet in the Mandalore sector that had been colonized by Mandalorians. Vizsla longed to restore the warrior heritage of the Mandalorians, and conspired with [[Count]] [[Dooku]] of the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Vizsla hoped the Republic would believe an intervention was necessary, so Death Watch could fight their invasion and be hailed by the Mandalorians as heroes. However, the plot failed, and the Galactic Senate rejected the [[Mandalore Defense Resolution]].<ref name="Duchess of Mandalore" />

The outcasts of Death Watch fled to become mercenaries, constructing a base on [[Carlac]]. The group began plotting for revenge, allying first with [[Separatist Senate|Separatist senator]] [[Lux Bonteri]] to plot Dooku's downfall,<ref name="A Friend in Need" /> and then with the renegade [[Sith Lord]] Maul's [[Shadow Collective]] to [[Takeover of Mandalore|win]] back the support of Mandalore's people.<ref name="Eminence">{{TCW|Eminence (episode)}}</ref> However, after Vizsla betrayed Maul, Maul killed him and became Death Watch's leader, prompting Bo-Katan Kryze to rebel against him, forming the [[Mandalore resistance]].<ref name="ShadesofReason" />

===New civil war===
{{Main|Mandalorian Civil War (19 BBY)}}
[[File:AlmecDeathWatch-ShadesOfReason.png|thumb|left|300px|Prime Minister Almec addresses the Mandalorians on Maul's behalf.]]
[[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] investigated the coup, but was captured, and Maul killed Satine to spite him. Kenobi escaped and returned to inform the Galactic Republic; in the meantime, [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]], secretly the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth]] Sidious, captured Maul and imprisoned him in the [[Spire (Stygeon Prime)|Spire]] on [[Stygeon Prime]].<ref name="The Lawless">{{TCW|The Lawless}}</ref> While Maul's [[Mandalorian super commando]]s proved to be loyal and [[Escape from the Spire|freed]] him,<ref name="SonOfDathomir1">[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 1|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 1]]</ref> his execution of Kryze was a rallying cry to many other Mandalorians, who allied together in the name of overthrowing Maul and returning Mandalore to Mandalorian control.<ref name="Who's Boss" />

Following the [[Siege of Mandalore]], Bo-Katan was named [[Regent]] of Mandalore,<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" /> leaving Maul's hold on Mandalore to collapse.<ref name="Out of Darkness">{{Rebels|Out of Darkness}}</ref> Eventually, Kryze was ousted out by [[Clan Saxon]] when she refused to follow [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] Palpatine,<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" /> and the planet was ultimately [[Occupation of Mandalore|occupied]] by the Galactic Empire.<ref name="Out of Darkness" /> Meanwhile, the Protectors, who regarded Death Watch as [[Treason|traitors]], not only assisted the [[Grand Army of the Republic]] in training [[clone trooper]]s,<ref name="The Protector of Concord Dawn" /> but also aided the Republic during the war. [[Skull Squadron]], a squadron of Protectors commanded by [[Fenn Rau]], assisted the Republic by training [[clone trooper pilot]]s and fought in the [[Third Battle of Mygeeto]].<ref name="Kanan 10">[[Kanan 10|''Kanan'' 10]]</ref>

===Age of the Empire===
====Under Imperial Rule====
{{Quote|He's the Emperor's Hand, the acting ruler and governor of Mandalore.|[[Tristan Wren]], on [[Gar Saxon]]|<ref name="Legacy of Mandalore" />}}
[[File:Gar_Saxon-FA.jpg|thumb|right|230px|Gar Saxon, Viceroy of Mandalore and the Emperor's Hand.]]
After the Imperial occupation of Mandalore, Rau's Protectors established a [[Protectors Camp|base]] on the third moon of Concord Dawn, getting paid by the Empire to protect their system on their behalf,<ref name="Protectors DB" /> while other Mandalorians would fall under the leadership of [[Gar Saxon]], with some of them joining in the [[Imperial Military]] as [[Imperial Super Commando]]s.<ref name="Imperial Super Commandos" /> Saxon, who had been appointed [[Viceroy]] of Mandalore by the Emperor, served as the [[Emperor's Hand|latter's Hand]] on the Mandalorian homeworld,<ref name="Legacy of Mandalore" /> enforcing the Empire's will alongside his fellow Imperial Super Commandos,<ref name="Imperial Super Commandos" /> which included his brother, Tiber Saxon.<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" />

[[File:Boba_Fett_OR.png|thumb|left|230px|Boba Fett, an infamous bounty hunter of Mandalorian heritage.]]
During the [[Imperial Era]], the [[Quarren]] criminal [[Lallani]] employed a gang of Mandalorians as mercenaries and guards.<ref name="Choose Your Destiny">''[[Choose Your Destiny: A Han & Chewie Adventure]]''</ref> Meanwhile, [[Boba Fett]], the [[Cloning|clone]] son<ref name="Boba DB">{{Databank|boba-fett|Boba Fett}}</ref> of the famed Mandalorian [[bounty hunter]] Jango Fett,<ref name="WOTBH IG-88" /> following his father's footsteps, had become known as the best bounty hunter in the galaxy, keeping the Mandalorian legacy alive by donning his father's [[Boba Fett's armor|distinctive]] Mandalorian armor.<ref name="Boba DB" /> Fett was eventually [[Rescue of Han Solo|defeated]] by the [[Heroes of Yavin]], and fell into the [[Great Pit of Carkoon]],<ref name="Episode VI">{{Film|VI}}</ref> though he managed to survive.<ref name="Chapter 12">{{BOBF|Chapter 1: Stranger in a Strange Land}}</ref>

Additionally, [[Sabine Wren]], who was a member of [[Clan Wren]], operated as a bounty hunter for a time, alongside fellow Mandalorian [[Ketsu Onyo]].<ref name="Blood Sisters">{{Rebels|Blood Sisters}}</ref> However, Sabine later became a member of a small [[Rebel cell/Canon|rebel cell]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] planet [[Lothal]],<ref name="SWR:TVG">''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> known as the [[Spectres]], who regularly raided the Imperials for supplies which they distributed to the needy,<ref name="The Siege of Lothal">''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Siege of Lothal]]''</ref> and later became part of a larger rebellion, the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="Secret Cargo">{{Rebels|Secret Cargo}}</ref> Years later, the Alliance would ally itself with several [[Mandalorian clan]]s during its [[Galactic Civil War|war]] with the Empire.<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" /><ref name="Zero Hour">{{Rebels|Zero Hour}}</ref><ref name="FLT" /> Meanwhile, Ketsu continued with her bounty hunter career, joining the [[Black Sun]] crime syndicate.<ref name="Blood Sisters" />

====Galactic Civil War====
{{Quote|If we had shown half that spine to the Empire we would've never lost our planet.|Bo-Katan Kryze, to Koska Reeves and Boba Fett|<ref name="Chapter 16">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}}</ref>}}
In [[2 BBY]], Gar Saxon and his Imperial Super [[Commando]]s wiped out the Mandalorian Protectors; as a result, Rau decided to join the rebellion.<ref name="Imperial Super Commandos" /> Later that year, Sabine Wren found the Darksaber on [[Dathomir]] after she, [[Kanan Jarrus]], and [[Ezra Bridger]] fought a battle there against Maul.<ref name="Visions and Voices">{{Rebels|Visions and Voices}}</ref> At the urging of Fenn and the rebel leaders [[Hera Syndulla]] and Jarrus, Sabine agreed to begin training with the Darksaber so that she could reunify her people and rally them to help the rebellion.<ref name="Trials of the Darksaber" />

[[File:YouAreSoGrounded-SWRS03E16.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Countess Ursa Wren meeting her daughter Sabine.]]
Following Sabine's training, she, Rau, Jarrus, and Bridger returned to Krownest to [[Wren Stronghold|Clan Wren's Stronghold]]. There, Sabine attempted to convince the clan's leader and her mother, Countess [[Ursa Wren]], to join the rebellion. At first, Ursa decided to surrender the Jedi to Viceroy Saxon and his Imperial Super Commandos in exchange for the Darksaber and sparing her daughter. When Saxon branded her and Clan Wren enemies of the Empire, Ursa and her son [[Tristan Wren|Tristan]] [[Skirmish on Krownest|fought]] Saxon and commandos alongside Rau and the Jedi. When Saxon tried to kill Ursa with the Darksaber, Sabine took [[Sabine Wren's lightsaber|Bridger's lightsaber]] and fought Saxon. Sabine was then able to reclaim the Darksaber and subdue Saxon. When Saxon tried to shoot Sabine, he was killed by Ursa. His death created a power vacuum among the Mandalorians. Sabine then decided to stay behind and help her mother, clan, and Rau find Mandalore's true leader, to whom she would give the Darksaber.<ref name="Legacy of Mandalore" />

Soon afterward, Bridger returned to Krownest, having escaped from the [[Battle of Atollon]], to request help from Clan Wren for the rebels against [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]], who was attacking the rebel base on [[Atollon]]. Although unable to send a full force, due to their current struggles against Clan Saxon, Ursa agreed to allow Sabine, Tristan, and Rau to lead several Mandalorian volunteers and ships to accompany Ezra and Chopper back to Atollon. The ''Gauntlet'' and several Fang fighters traveled back to Atollon, where they destroyed the [[Interdictor]] vessel that was preventing the rebels from escaping. Able to escape, the remaining rebels fled the system, while the Mandalorians returned to Krownest.<ref name="Zero Hour" />

[[File:SWR_S4_Mandalore_Civil_War_1.png|thumb|left|250px|Two warring groups of Mandalorians aligned on opposite sides of the Galactic Civil War fought for control of Mandalore.]]
In [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Chronology Note HOM">{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/heroes-of-mandalore-trivia-gallery|text="Heroes of Mandalore" Trivia Gallery}} of the trivia gallery for ''[[Star Wars Rebels: Heroes of Mandalore]]'' states Bo-Katan Kryze's character model has been aged by 18 [[Standard year|years]] or so. The last time Kryze was seen was in [[19 BBY]] in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode "[[The Lawless]]," which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates to 19 BBY.</ref> Clan Wren under the leadership of Ursa and Sabine fought on Mandalore against Clan Saxon and the Empire. At some point during the Mandalorian civil war, Sabine and her younger brother, Tristan, arrived at the statue of Tarre Vizsla and discovered that the Empire had built an outpost situated on it. Sabine and Tristan destroyed the outpost and restored the statue to its original state.<ref name="Art History" /> Clan Wren was joined by several other factions and clans including the sole Journeyman Protector Rau, [[Lady]] Bo-Katan's [[Clan Kryze]], [[Clan Vizsla]], [[Clan Rook]], and [[Clan Eldar]]. Sabine and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance's]] Spectres Jarrus and Bridger also [[Mission to Mandalore|attacked]] an [[Mandalore prison outpost|Imperial prison]] hoping to find [[Alrich Wren]], although Alrich had been moved.<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" />

Sabine then offered Kryze the Darksaber, but she refused knowing she was not the leader her sister, Satine, had been. Together they attacked a [[convoy]] guarded by the super commandos. They were then able to rescue Alrich. However, the commandos and the Empire then deployed an [[AT-DP Arc Cannon Prototype|AT-DP]] armed with the "[[Arc Pulse Generator|the Duchess]]" weapon prototype that disintegrated numerous warriors of Clans Wren and Kryze. Only Tristan and Ursa survived the onslaught. The survivors then regrouped. Sabine and Bo-Katan then planned to destroy it by sneaking aboard Governor Tiber Saxon's [[Tiber Saxon's Star Destroyer|Star Destroyer]] near Sundari to atone for her role in creating the weapon.<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" />

The combined Mandalorian and rebel forces managed to infiltrate Saxon's Star Destroyer. Following a skirmish, they destroyed the ''Duchess'' and Saxon's vessel. After the battle, Lady Bo-Katan assumed the Darksaber and the mantle of leadership over the Mandalorian clans. The Vizslas, Wrens, Kryzes, Rooks, Eldars, and the sole remaining Protector, Fenn Rau, pledged allegiance to the new Mand'alor.<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" /> The rogue Children of the Watch were appalled that Kryze had taken the Darksaber as a gift instead of winning it in combat, believing it cursed their world to fall.<ref name="Return of the Mandalorian" />

At some point, the Rebel Alliance received help from the Old Mandalorian faction; a [[Vlemoth Port battalion|battalion]] of Mandalorians from [[Vlemoth Port]] aided Rebel forces against an Imperial [[Ralchio Nervi's task force|task force]] led by [[Ralchio Nervi]] during the [[Battle of Xorrn]].<ref name="FLT" /> Much like Fenn Rau, Mandalorians [[Bodica Venj]] and [[Dirk Ullodin]] fought for the rebels. Venj was a wrathful Mandalorian warrior who once flew a Fang fighter on approach to the Wren Stronghold on Krownest during their service to the rebels, while Ullodin wanted to become a commando and, at some point during their rebel service, took part in a space battle, where they flew a Fang fighter and shot down a TIE fighter.<ref name="Pride of Mandalore">{{Twitter|atomicmassgames|status/1481303335617581064|Atomic Mass Games|quote=A host of skilled Mandalorians – including ace Fenn Rau – bring the Fang Fighter to the Rebel Alliance in the Pride of Mandalore Reinforcements Pack for #StarWarsXWing. ====Great Purge of Mandalore====
{{Main|Great Purge of Mandalore}}
{{Quote|I did surrender. After our forces were annihilated in the Night of a Thousand Tears and defeat was imminent, I met with Moff Gideon. The ISB had reached out to me to negotiate a cease-fire. In exchange for submitting to the Empire and disarming, all remaining cities and Mandalorian lives were to be spared. That is how Moff Gideon came to possess the Darksaber. I didn't trust him, but it was the only chance I had to save our people. And then he betrayed me and we were helpless to resist the Purge of Mandalore.|Bo-Katan Kryze|<ref name="Ch. 23" />}}
[[File:KX-droids-Mandalore-Purge.png|thumb|right|310px|KX-series security droids massacre Mandalorian survivors during the "Night of a Thousand Tears."]]
Kryze's reign as Mand'alor was short lived. Realizing they would never be able to control Mandalore and wanting to make sure no other faction could, the Empire instead launched [[Great Purge of Mandalore]],<ref name="Chapter 11" /> killing millions of Mandalorians. During the purge, Mandalore was heavily bombed in the [[Night of a Thousand Tears]].<ref name="Return of the Mandalorian" /> The Children of the Watch<ref name="Chapter 11" /> avoided the Purge, as they were cloistered on Concordia.<ref name="Return of the Mandalorian" />

With the destruction of most of her forces in the Night, Kryze was forced to agree to a ceasefire talk proposed by the [[Imperial Security Bureau]] on the belief that surrender was the only way her people could survive. While she did not trust him, Kryze met with<ref name="Ch. 23" /> an ISB [[officer]] named [[Gideon]]<ref name="Chapter 11" /> and surrendered the Darksaber, further agreeing to disarm her people and submit to the Empire in return for an end to the fighting. However, Gideon betrayed her. The Empire continued the Purge against the defenseless-Mandalore<ref name="Ch. 23" /> and almost totally destroy the Mandalorian people.<ref name="Return of the Mandalorian" />

===New Republic Era===
====Hunt for Grogu====
{{Main|Hunt for Grogu}}
{{Quote|When one chooses to walk the Way of the Mandalore, you are both hunter and prey. How can one be a coward if one chooses this way of life?|A Mandalorian armorer|<ref name="Chapter 3" />}}
[[File:The-Tribe-Manga.png|thumb|left|300px|A tribe, known simply as "the Tribe," went into hiding after the Great Purge.]]
Following the Great Purge, surviving Mandalorians went into hiding,<ref name="Chapter 3" /> and the Mandalorian people were believed to have perished completely.<ref name="Chapter 6" /> In the years following the [[Battle of Jakku|fall]] of the Empire, the once-great warriors became fewer and fewer, and beskar also became rarer and rarer.<ref name="Besker Databank">{{Databank|beskar|beskar}}</ref>

By circa [[9 ABY]],<ref name="MandoDate">{{MandoDate}}</ref> a [[The Tribe|Mandalorian tribe]] affiliated with the [[Children of the Watch]]<ref name="Chapter 11" /> was hiding in a [[Nevarro Mandalorian covert|covert]] on [[Nevarro]], a world in the outer reaches of the galaxy. One of its members was the bounty hunter [[Din Djarin]], known as "the Mandalorian." After Djarin did business with an [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|Imperial remnant]], it caused a disturbance within the covert, with one member, [[Paz Vizsla]] of [[Clan Vizsla]],<ref name="Return of the Mandalorian" /> calling Djarin a coward for dealing with the Imperials.<ref name="Chapter 3" />

Soon after the confrontation as well as a conversation with a Mandalorian known as "[[the Armorer]]," Djarin decided to go against the remnant and rescue [[Din Grogu|Grogu]], an infantile member of [[Yoda's species]] whom he had captured and turned over to the Imperial remnant. However, after he performed a rescue, he was stopped by the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]], who sought good relations with the local Imperials. Then, Mandalorians from the covert emerged from hiding and [[Incident on Nevarro|fought against]] the Bounty Hunters' Guild, protecting one of their own. Djarin escaped, but, as a result of openly fighting, the Tribe was forced to relocate the covert.<ref name="Chapter 3" />

[[File:DinDjarinBlasterPistol-TMS01E01.png|thumb|right|250px|Din Djarin, a renowned Mandalorian bounty hunter.]]
Despite the attempts of the Tribe to relocate the covert, a large majority of them had been [[Attack on the Tribe|killed]] by [[Moff]] Gideon's Imperial remnant. The Armorer was among those who survived, and it was speculated that others escaped Nevarro. When Djarin returned to Nevarro, the Armorer established "[[Clan Mudhorn]]" as Din Djarin's clan, consisting of Djarin and Grogu. Djarin was then tasked to reunite Grogu with the Jedi Order.<ref name="Chapter 8" /> Vizsla survived the attack as well.<ref name="Return of the Mandalorian" />

During this time, Lady Kryze and two of [[Bo-Katan Kryze's unit|her followers]], [[Koska Reeves]] and [[Axe Woves]], were highjacking Imperial shipments on [[Trask]]. Their goal was to use the shipments to reclaim Mandalore and have Kryze reinstated as the Mand'alor. Kryze also enlisted the aid of Djarin in exchange for locating a surviving Jedi—Ahsoka Tano. With Djarin's help, Kryze and her followers were able to take the cruiser and its cargo. Unfortunately, the cruiser's [[Unidentified Imperial captain|captain]] refused to reveal the location of the Darksaber and took his own life.<ref name="Chapter 11" />

[[File:Mando3-Bostrikes.png|thumb|left|250px|Bo-Katan Kryze and her followers attack Quarren fishermen to save Din Djarin.]]
After helping Kryze, Djarin continued with his quest to return Grogu with the Jedi Order,<ref name="Chapter 11" /> protecting his foundling from several bounty hunters that were [[Hunt for Grogu|hunting]] the [[youngling]],<ref name="Chapter 3" /> as well as from Gideon's Imperial remnant. Despite Djarin's efforts, Gideon eventually succeeded in [[Battle of Tython (9 ABY)|capturing]] Grogu, forcing Djarin to ask out his allies to help him rescue Grogu.<ref name="Chapter 14" /> Djarin assembled a team consisting of [[New Republic]] [[Marshal]] [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]], [[Master Assassin]] [[Fennec Shand]], and Boba Fett.<ref name="Chapter 15">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 15: The Believer}}</ref> Djarin and Fett also met with Kryze and Reeves on the [[desert]] [[planet]] of [[Lafete]], asking the [[Nite Owls]] for help in [[Second rescue of Grogu|boarding]] [[Gideon's light cruiser]]. After a brief fight between Reeves and Fett, the latter who had felt insulted by the Nite Owls' comments on his [[Cloning|clone]] origin, Kryze agreed to help Djarin, since she wished to retrieve the Darksaber from Gideon.<ref name="Chapter 16" />

With the Nite Owls' help, Djarin's team was able take control of the cruiser. However, Djarin had taken the Darksaber from Gideon, but could not to give it to Kryze freely.<ref name="Chapter 16" /> The forces Kryze had gathered, including Reeves, rejected her once she returned without the Darksaber<ref name="Ch.17" /> and struck out under Woves as mercenaries for hire.<ref name="Chapter 22" />

====War for Tatooine====
{{Quote|The way I see it, we have two choices. We wait until they get into position and launch a siege on their terms.''"<br />"''Or?''"<br />"''We rush out there, catch them unaware. Then we can escape to your ship at the palace.''"<br />"''I can't abandon Mos Espa. These people are counting on me.''"<br />"''Okay, then. We'll both die in the name of honor.|Din Djarin and Boba Fett|<ref name="In the Name of Honor">{{BOBF|Chapter 7: In the Name of Honor}}</ref>}}
After rescuing Grogu and reuniting him with the Jedi Order, Djarin continued his career as a bounty hunter, while Boba Fett went to [[Tatooine]] to establish his [[Fett gotra|own]] [[gotra]], coming into conflict with the [[Pyke Syndicate]], a powerful faction of the [[Spice Cartel]].<ref name="The Streets of Mos Espa">{{BOBF|Chapter 3: The Streets of Mos Espa}}</ref>

[[File:MandoCombo-BoBFCh7.png|thumb|right|300px|Boba Fett and Din Djarin during the Battle for Mos Espa.]]
After completing a mission on [[Glavis Ringworld]], Djarin rejoined the survivors of his tribe at a [[Mandalorian covert|new covert]], where the Armorer recounted the Purge and reforged his [[beskar spear]] into an [[Grogu's chainmail shirt|armor]] for Grogu. Djarin was challenged and [[Fight for the Darksaber|dueled]] Paz Vizsla, a descendant of Tarre Vizsla, for ownership of the Darksaber, and managed to defeat his rival. However, he was expelled from the Tribe for removing his helmet, which was against the [[Way of the Mandalore]], the tribe's way of life. According to Creed, the only way for him to be redeemed was in the [[Living Waters]] beneath the [[Mines of Mandalore]], which he thought to be destroyed. After this, Djarin also made his way to Tatooine, where he was hired by Boba Fett to aid him in his [[War against the Pykes|war]] against the Pykes.<ref name="Return of the Mandalorian" />

Fett and Djarin fought together against the Pyke forces during the [[Battle of Mos Espa]], and it was during the battle that Djarin was reunited with his foundling Grogu, who had decided to return to Djarin, instead of continuing his [[Jedi training]]. Eventually, the Pykes were defeated by the Fett gotra, securing the Fett gotra's position as the leading criminal organization of Tatooine, while Djarin and Grogu left the planet.<ref name="In the Name of Honor" />

====All roads lead to Mandalore====
=====New covert=====
[[File:Airbourne-Paz-CH17.png|thumb|left|300px|The Mandalorian Tribe defends itself against an attacking lake monster during Ragnar's initiation.]]
Despite Vizsla's fear that he, Djarin, and the Armorer were the only survivors of their clan,<ref name="Return of the Mandalorian" /> other survivors of the Tribe would re-surface. The Armorer's tribe was able to re-establish itself<ref name="Ch. 21">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 21: The Pirate}}</ref> as a covert at a new [[Mandalorian secret covert|location]] on a [[Armorer's planet|planet]], where they were led by the Armorer once more.<ref name="Ch.17">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 17: The Apostate}}</ref> Vizsla and his foundling son [[Ragnar Vizsla|Ragnar]] were amongst the group.<ref name="Chapter 20" /> During Ragnar's [[Mandalorian initiation ritual|initiation ritual]], the covert came under [[Skirmish outside a Mandalorian covert|attack]] by a [[lake monster]]. Several Mandalorians were eaten by the turtle until Djarin killed it with his [[N-1 starfighter|N-1]] [[Din Djarin's N-1 starfighter|starfighter]]. Djarin, despite being an [[Apostate (religion)|apostate]], spoke with the Armorer about traveling to Mandalore to find the mines and redeem himself. The Armorer agreed to allow him to go on his quest. Following a run-in with several [[pirate]]s belonging to [[Pirate King]] [[Gorian Shard]]'s [[Gorian Shard's pirate crew|gang]] of the [[Pirate Nation]], Djarin traveled to Kalevala. There, he spoke with Kryze about returning to Mandalore. However, she declined since she refused to take the Darksaber from Djarin and was abandoned by her forces to become mercenaries for hire. She chose to stay in exile at [[Kryze Fortress|Kryze Castle]].<ref name="Ch.17" />

Djarin, Grogu, and [[R5-D4]] traveled to Mandalore. Once there, they ventured into the ruins of Sundari where the three of them ran into trouble from [[Alamite]]s. Djarin was captured by a [[Cyborg mech|cyborg]] [[scavenger]] and its [[Spider Tank]]. Grogu was able to escape it and the alamites back to the Djarin's starfighter which was piloted by R5. Grogu was able to convince Kryze to help him rescue Djarin. Together, they were able to get past the alamites and was able to use the Darksaber to kill the cyborg and its tank.<ref name="Ch. 18" />

Kryze then took Djarin to the Mines and the Living Waters. There, Djarin was able to redeem himself. However he tripped and fell deep into the water. Kryze jumped in after. In the waters, Kryze discovered a mythosaur.<ref name="Ch. 18">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 18: The Mines of Mandalore}}</ref> After filling a flask with some of the Living Waters, Djarin, Kryze and Grogu left. Kryze and Djarin went to Kalevala to retrieve his fighter. However, Kryze came under attack by several [[TIE/IN interceptor]]s. Djarin and Kryze were able to destroy several interceptors. However, another group of [[TIE/sa tactical bomber|TIE/sa bombers]] destroyed Kryze Castle. Kryze, distraught, went after the bombers. However, a dozen more interceptors came. Djarin was able to convince her to retreat and follow her to his covert's planet.<ref name="Ch. 19">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 19: The Convert}}</ref>

Upon their arrival at the covert, Djarin and Kryze were looked on as apostates until the Armorer confirmed that they truly been to Living Waters of Mandalore. Djarin was accepted and Kryze, despite not believing in the Children of the Watch's beliefs, was accepted into their covert.<ref name="Ch. 19" /> During the covert's training of its children, Ragnar was taken by a [[shriek-hawk]]. Kryze led Djarin, Vizsla, and several others to rescue Ragnar. They were successful and captured the shriek-hawk's children. During this time, the Armorer forge new armor for Grogu and a new pauldron for Kryze to signify her discovery of a mythosaur.<ref name="Chapter 20" />

=====Fighting the Pirate Nation at Nevarro=====
The covert was then approached by [[Adelphi Rangers]]' Captain [[Carson Teva]] of the New Republic. Their location was revealed by Djarin's astromech, R5. At first, Djarin and his covert were hesitant to hear the captain until he told them of [[High Magistrate]] Karga's and Nevarro's attack by Pirate King Shard's gang. Following Captain Teva's departure, Djarin and Kryze spoke with the covert's members about helping Nevarro.<ref name="Ch. 21" /> Despite fighting several of Karga's guild hunters that forced them to relocate the covert<ref name="Chapter 3" />, Vizsla and the others agreed to help Djarin in fighting Shard's pirates.<ref name="Ch. 21" />

With [[Bo-Katan Kryze's Gauntlet starfighter|Kryze's Gauntlet starfighter]] and Djarin's starfighter, the Mandalorians were able to fight the pirates and drive them from both the city and [[Nevarro sewer|Nevarro]]. In gratitude for their actions, High Magistrate Karga gave the Tribe lands they could call their own for the first time in years. Shortly after, Kryze was summoned by the Armorer at the covert's former workshop. The Armorer allowed Kryze to take off her helmet,<ref name="Ch. 21" /> saying that due to her seeing a mythosaur,<ref name="Ch. 18" /> the time had come for all Mandalorians to reunite and reclaim Mandalore. Thus, Kryze, Djarin, Grogu, and R5 set off to find Kryze's fleet and reunite both Mandalorian tribes.<ref name="Ch. 21" />

=====Privateers on Plazir-15=====
During this time, Woves and other Mandalorians were using Gideon's light cruiser to carry out mercenary work in the Mid Rim territories. One mission involving Woves' Mandalorians capturing Captain [[Shuggoth]]'s [[Unidentified Mon Calamari viceroy's son|lover]] in order to return him to his parent, a [[Unidentified Mon Calamari viceroy|Mon Calamari Viceroy]].<ref name="Chapter 22" />

Woves and his fellow privateers also accepted a job to protect the pacifist planet of [[Plazir-15]] led by the [[the Duchess]] and her husband, Captain [[Bombardier (individual)|Bombardier]]. Kryz and Djarin arrived and helped the Duchess and Captain in stopping a former Separatist, [[Commissioner]] [[Helgait]], from turning Plazir's droid workforce back into battle droids. Djarin and Kryze met up with Woves and his Mandalorians in an attempt to reclaim her leadership position. After a brief fight between Kryze and Woves, Djarin gave the Darksaber back to Kryze, due to her rescuing him from a cyborg on Mandalore, thus making him unworthy to hold the saber according to the Mandalorian code, with Woves and his fellow Mandalorians accepting Kryze as their leader once more.<ref name="Chapter 22" />

===Reconquest of Mandalore===
After uniting Kryze's unit and Djarin's tribe, the Mandalorian fleet traveled to Mandalore. A small scouting team led by Kryze and Djarin was sent to surveil the ground. On the planet's surface, they met with [[Mandalorian survivors|Mandalorians]] who had survived on their own since the Great Purge of Mandalore. This group of survivors led the scouting team to the Great Forge. Upon arriving to the forge, they were ambushed by Gideon's [[Imperial armored commando|armored commandos]] and led into a trap inside a [[Mandalore Imperial base|hidden Imperial base]] where Gideon, clad in [[Dark Trooper phase 4|Mandalorian-style beskar armor]], attempted to force the surrender of the Mandalorians. However, they managed to escape with Vizla staying behind to allow the rest to escape, with him being killed by three [[Praetorian Guard|Imperial Praetorian Guards]] shortly after.<ref name="Ch. 23" />

Woves went into orbit and alerted the fleet about the incoming TIE interceptors and bombers. He ordered all the Mandalorians on board their Imperial light cruiser to evacuate. Woves then piloted the light cruiser as bait for the Imperials while the rest went on to reinforce their brethren on the ground. While the Mandalorians and the Imperial commandos engaged in aerial combat, Djarin, Kryze, and Grogu dueled Gideon. In the middle of the battle, Gideon managed to destroy the Darksaber using his armor's mechanized strength. However, with their united efforts, Gideon and his forces were defeated just before their former light cruiser crashed into the base, killing Gideon and whatever remained of his forces, with Grogu using the Force to protect Djarin and Kryze from the blast. Shortly after the battle, Mandalorians gathered at the Living Waters to witness Ragnar Vizla and Grogu becoming Mandalorian apprentices. A ceremony was later held to reignite the Great Forge, signifying the reclamation of their homeworld as a united people.<ref name="Chapter 24">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 24: The Return}}</ref>

==Mandalorians in the galaxy==
===Galactic influence===
{{Quote|Never get between a Mandalorian and a weapons package.|Sabine Wren|<ref name="Wings of the Master" />}}
Mandalorians were known across the stars as the greatest warriors the galaxy had ever created,<ref name="Chapter 6" /> with even their armor alone striking fear in the hearts of many across the galaxy.<ref name="DeathWatchDB" /> During the [[Clone Wars]], the [[Trandoshan]] [[big game hunter]] [[Garnac]] kept a [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders|Mandalorian Neo-Crusader]] helmet as a trophy.<ref name="WH TG" /> Boba Fett, a human male bounty hunter of Mandalorian heritage, wore armor inherited from his father [[Jango Fett]], a famed Mandalorian bounty hunter<ref name="WOTBH IG-88" /> raised as a foundling,<ref name="Chapter 14" /> keeping the memory of the Mandalorians alive well into the [[Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Boba Fett">{{Databank|boba-fett|Boba Fett}}</ref> Jango's armor inspired [[Phase I clone trooper armor|those]] of the soldiers cloned from him, starting a design lineage that continued down to the [[First Order stormtrooper|stormtroopers]] of the [[First Order]].<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" />

===After the Great Purge===
{{Quote|Our people are scattered like stars in the galaxy. What are we? What do we stand for?|Din Djarin, after the Great Purge|<ref name="Ch. 18" />}}
[[File:Card-Trader-Where-I-Go-He-Goes.png|thumb|right|250px|As a Clan of Two, Din Djarin with his ward Grogu traveled the galaxy after the Great Purge.]]
Following the Great Purge, the majority of the Mandalorians had been killed,<ref name="Chapter 6" /> making them a rare sight in the galaxy. One group known as "the Tribe" survived and hid on Nevarro,<ref name="Chapter 3" /> but many were exterminated by an Imperial remnant. Afterward, Din Djarin was tasked with searching the galaxy for Grogu's species as their own clan.<ref name="Chapter 8" /> The Armorer and Paz Vizsla were able to regroup on [[Glavis Ringworld]]<ref name="Return of the Mandalorian" /> and eventually rejoin other survivors of the Tribe on a [[Armorer's planet|planet]],<ref name="Ch. 21" /> where they would later be joined by Djarin, Grogu, and Bo-Katan Kryze.<ref name="Ch. 19" /> The gathered Mandalorian tribe would later move to Nevarro once more and, reuniting with Kryze's former followers, took part in the reconquest and resettlement of Mandalore.<ref name="Chapter 24" />

The last of [[Clan Tal]] after his fellow Mandalorians were wiped out in the Great Purge, the Mandalorian [[Aran Tal]] fought in the [[Hunters of the Outer Rim]] competition. He once declared that, with the loss of Mandalore and his clan, it was his responsibility to maintain the traditions of all his fellow Mandalorians.<ref name="Hunters">''[[Star Wars: Hunters]]''</ref> Several Mandalorian war banners decorated the entrance of [[Maz Kanata]]'s [[Takodana Castle|castle]] on the planet [[Takodana]].<ref name="Complete Locations">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref>

Glut]]. As mentioned in the novelization, the Mandalorians were now imagined as "a group of evil warriors defeated by the Jedi Knights during the Clone Wars."<ref name="ESB novel">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref>

When it came time to introduce the Mandalorians in [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|season two]] of [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'']], [[George Lucas]] and [[Dave Filoni]] looked at the Mandalorians in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity and decided to keep the broad strokes of their history. Filoni wanted to give the Mandalorian people's appearance a "Nordic flavor." ''The Clone Wars'' art department looked at Fett's armor and translated its angles, particularly the diamond shape on the breastplate, into every aspect of the Mandalorian aesthetic. Filoni and Lucas felt it should be made clear that the ancient Mandalorians were an [[army]], not a ragtag band of warriors wearing customized armor, so Death Watch would look uniform. (The decision also kept Boba Fett's armor unique.) Filoni hoped to eventually show how the Mandalorians became mercenaries who supplied Fett with his unusual armor.<ref name="Creating Mandalore" /> When Death Watch reappeared in [[The Clone Wars: Season Four|season four's]] "[[A Friend in Need]]," the characters were given a greater variety of gear, lending them what Lucas described as a "biker gang feel."<ref name="A Friend in Need Trivia">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/a-friend-in-need-trivia-gallery|text="A Friend in Need" Trivia Gallery}}</ref>

Before its cancellation, ''The Clone Wars'' was to depict the Siege of Mandalore. Writer [[Henry Gilroy]] said Mandalore was likely occupied by the Republic before it turned into the Empire. He speculated due to Mandalore's importance, it was likely a "soft occupation," with a new Mandalorian puppet leader ruling the planet.<ref name="RebelsRecon212" /> ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' has since confirmed that the Mandalorian named Bo-Katan Kryze became Regent of Mandalore following the Siege, and was deposed by Emperor Palpatine following the end of the Republic.<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" /> The Siege was later depicted in [[The Clone Wars: Season Seven|''The Clone Wars'' revival]] on [[Disney+]].<ref name="Old Friends">{{TCW|Old Friends Not Forgotten}}</ref>
